scope: Modern continuous hair only: asymmetric swept support volume, broader combed locks and connected long-hair back/side curtain. Not complete portrait naturalism or population calibration.
doneCondition: Modern combed/long hair has visible form changes in matched front, three-quarter and profile captures.
Saved recipes, non-hair geometry and categorical legacy geometry remain exact versus the accepted pre-change face renderer.
Continuous boundaries remain bounded and all tested meshes stay within existing resource limits.
Built worker/in-page clients preserve front/profile head images, natural identity, body measurements and RNG through named-save replacement/load/reload.

testCorrection.reason: Two historical hair tests compared current full head anatomy to references predating the independently accepted chin/eye/face changes. Their current compatibility authority now uses the accepted face renderer frozen before this scalp change.

findings: Matched parted hair has more sweep, rooted clump structure and less uniform cap volume.
Long hair now occupies back/side space down to the jaw and below; previous cheek-height sparse wires were rejected.
Faces still look stylized/plastic and long-hair materials/ends need further craft; body naturalism and full rendered mass accounting also remain unfinished.

repair.finding: Nonperiodic asymmetric scalp support and unwrapped curtain roots.
repair.change: Modern scalp angles normalize to a single periodic domain; front-weighted asymmetry returns to symmetric rear support. Actual emitted rear positions/normals now meet across every row in twelve extreme combinations.
